releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.21.1
releases.body:
## Fixes

- **Linux AppImage: model checks no longer create stray projects.** The dashboard asks OpenCode which models are available. On a Linux AppImage, those checks ran inside the AppImage's temporary mount folder, so OpenCode saw that folder as a new project each time. They now run from Magic Context's data folder, or your home folder when the data folder setting is blank or relative. Thanks to the reporter of issue #964 for the fix.

# v0.49.76

This patch fixes a set of bugs found in a review of the plugins for OpenCode, Pi and Oh My Pi. It also fixes a slowdown in the experimental Rust mode on very large sessions.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: `/btw` could send the old text of a message you had edited.** A side question replays the conversation it was asked in. If you edited the last message it covered, and OpenCode's edit event arrived late, the replay could still send the text from before the edit. That includes text you removed on purpose. The replay now checks every message it sends against what OpenCode holds, including attachments, and skips the replay when anything differs. Hidden maintenance runs no longer prepare a replay at all, and the check is about 30% faster on long sessions.
- **`/ctx-wrapup` could report success and then not apply.** A wrap-up lets the next message apply the new summary. If another write to the same session's history happened at the same moment, the next message could send the old history, and the wrap-up was used up anyway. The summary then waited for an unrelated rebuild. The wrap-up now stays pending until a request actually carries its summary, on OpenCode 1, OpenCode 2, Pi and Oh My Pi. It is also used up when the history it raced with already includes the summary, so it never costs an extra cache rewrite.
- **Near the context limit, the emergency drop ignored images it removed.** When it turns a recent tool call into a short placeholder, the call's images go too. The drop did not count that saving. It could then keep a large screenshot and drop more tool outputs than it needed to. It now counts exactly what each drop removes.
- **OpenCode 2: automated host messages counted differently after a restart.** Messages OpenCode marks as automated were counted as your own messages in a live session, but not after OpenCode restored the session from a checkpoint. That shifted when older tool outputs were cleaned up. Both paths now treat them as automated.
- **Pi and Oh My Pi: screenshots counted at full size when judging how old a tool output is.** Old tool outputs are cleaned up once enough newer conversation follows them. A screenshot the model no longer sees, or that a text-only model never sees, counted as about 1,200 tokens of newer conversation. Images now count at what is actually sent.
- **Semantic memory search could keep retrying the same memories.** When some memories had no stored embedding, each search tried the same first 50 again. Memories after them never got an embedding, so a search by meaning could not find them. Each search now continues where the last one stopped, and the limits per search are unchanged.
- **Docs upkeep dropped corrections to oversized docs.** When a project's docs were already over the size budget, the nightly docs task dropped every proposed edit, even one that made the docs shorter. Edits that keep the size or shrink it are now kept.
- **Experimental Rust mode: very large sessions could time out.** One planning step scanned every message once for each assistant reply. On a session of about 31 MB it took over 90 seconds, so the request ran out of time. It now builds a lookup once and takes about 5 seconds.

# v0.49.75

This patch fixes `doctor --fix` for Pi, which could delete files outside Magic Context's caches. Upgrade before you run `doctor --fix` or `doctor --force` again.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **`doctor --fix` for Pi could delete a linked folder's contents:** while looking for old copies of Magic Context in Pi's caches, doctor followed linked folders. If a project's Pi package folder was a link to a checkout, which a local or linked install creates, doctor walked into that checkout. When the checkout held an older Magic Context version, doctor deleted it as a stale cache. Doctor no longer follows links when it looks for caches. Before it clears anything, it checks that the folder is a real folder inside the cache, with no linked folder on the way, and it checks again right before it deletes. A folder that fails the check is left alone, and doctor says so. The same check now guards every cache doctor clears: Pi, Oh My Pi, OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2. Real stale caches are still cleared as before.
- **`doctor --fix` for Pi treated a beta or other tagged install as stale:** with Pi set to `@cortexkit/pi-magic-context@beta` (or another tag), doctor compared the installed copy with the `latest` release and deleted it when they differed, even when the installed copy was newer. Doctor now looks up the tag you chose and clears only a copy that is older than it, as the OpenCode 2 check already did. When it can't tell which version you want, it keeps your installed copy.

# v0.49.74

This patch fixes two cases where Magic Context could act on stale text: an OpenCode 2 side question after you edit an earlier message, and nightly memory verification after a memory is corrected mid-run.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2 side questions could resend a message you had edited (#971, thanks @iceteaSA):** a side question reuses the prompt Magic Context last prepared, so it stays on the cached prefix. After you edited or reverted an earlier message, a side question asked before your next normal turn could still carry the old text. Magic Context now drops the saved prompt when a message is edited or reverted. It also checks that the history before the newest message is unchanged before reusing the saved prompt; the check hashes image bytes directly, so long sessions with many images stay fast. When nothing was edited, side questions send exactly the same bytes as before.
- **Nightly memory verification could undo a correction made while it ran (#972, thanks @iceteaSA):** verification shows the model a batch of memories, which can take minutes. If an agent corrected one of those memories in the meantime, an "update" or "archive" answer was still applied to it, replacing the correction or archiving it. Every answer is now applied only if the memory still has the text the model checked; otherwise it's skipped and checked again on a later run.

# v0.49.73

This patch makes `/ctx-wrapup` shrink the prompt on your next message, and stops it from planning with the wrong context window after a restart.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin and restart OpenCode, Pi or Oh My Pi. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **`/ctx-wrapup` didn't shrink the prompt until the next rebuild (#967, thanks @JohanTG):** below the execute threshold, a finished wrapup saved its new summaries, but the next request still carried every raw message they covered. The summaries only reached the model at the next natural rebuild, which could be many turns later. A successful wrapup now applies its new history on the very next message, as `/ctx-flush` does: the summaries come in and the covered raw messages leave the request. The cached baseline isn't rebuilt. A wrapup that adds no summaries changes nothing. If the host restarts before your next message, the summaries apply at the next rebuild instead, and the completion message says so.
- **`/ctx-wrapup` planned with a 128,000-token window after a restart (#967):** when no model had been used yet in the running host, the command sized its chunks for a 128,000-token window, which made a wrapup on a large-window session take far longer than needed. It now uses the session's selected or last model and that model's real window, and refuses with a clear message when no window is known.
